result.addendumClause: V·§App-shell (MT-APP-1, adjudicated worker-F 2026-07-27) — NORMATIVE. The application entry is a module file, never inline HTML: it installs the router, awaits router.isReady(), and mounts into a dedicated container that is not <body>; no component renders a route-derived pane before the route is true, and no boot beat is armed by a single cancelable DOM event without a state-checked arm. Pane-instance registration rides the slot's own identity (liveKey) on every call site at every viewport — a slot that can mount without registering, or a breakpoint branch that can omit registration, is malformed; all pane-instance plumbing is typed (InstanceType unions; `any` in the shell seam is a defect). The route/view/component lattice has exactly one home (VIEW_MAP), routes derive from it, unknown names are navigation events not silent substitutions, and componentFor is exhaustive over the closed union. The shell owns exactly one <main>, one document H1, a skip link first in tab order, and one polite role=status region that announces redirects; a boot may not write the address bar with state no user action produced. The dual-pane retirement, ratio law, document-scroll, and chassis adoption remain governed by the VISUAL-CONSTITUTION's member-composition program and are NOT discharged by this wave; their ids (D-2, D-3, D-7, D-8, D-14) travel there un-renamed. Two owners of 'read the colour out of the URL' and one of them is inert at boot. boot/hydrate.ts is the pure synchronous seed resolver reading `location.hash` (header lines 1-30, and it is explicit that it owns the FIRST value); useColorUrl.ts:25-47 reads `route.query.space/color` and :71 runs `const appliedFromUrl = applyUrlToModel()` during App setup. Vue Router 4's initial navigation is asynchronous — `router.isReady()` at useViewManager.ts:41 is a Promise — so `route.query` is the START_LOCATION's empty object at setup and `applyUrlToModel()` always returns false. This did not survive re-derivation. Both arms. The challenger labelled this a HYPOTHESIS and declined to admit its own frame, which is correct discipline; but the source-side claim it rested on is false, and I checked the bytes myself rather than taking anyone's word. demo/styles/foundation.css:678 opens `@media (forced-colors: active)` and its tier-1 selector list at :680-696 explicitly names `canvas`, `.atmosphere-canvas` AND `[data-glass-field-canvas]` — the exact stamp App.vue:16 applies to the aurora canvas — with `forced-color-adjust: none`. The strongest row in the set, and I reproduced it independently before believing it. Control cold load of /#/ at 1440×900: marks `[b0,b1,b3,b2,b4]`, `.hero-blob-anchor` present. Ten of fourteen routes have a non-picker left pane. This is the wave's second gate.

Same defect as D-1, arrived at from the implementation side rather than the design side, and every structural citation checks out: App.vue:83-91 is the only PaneSlot call site without `:on-mount`; App.vue:105 and :131 carry it; App.vue:323-332 are the sole writers of the four refs; PaneSlot.vue:124 attaches `:ref` only when `onMount` is supplied, so at mobile the mounted component is never captured at all. I record the convergence rather than counting it twice: C-2 and D-1 are one row seen by two blind seats, which is exactly the independent-rediscovery evidence L-14 says is the only verifier this repository's history shows working. MT-W-APP-1 books them as a single carry with both identifiers preserved (L-5 anti-rename), and gate G4 discharges both.

Two arms, different evidentiary strength, and I separate them rather than accept the pair. The re-fire arm is CONFIRMED by construction: PaneSlot.vue:124 is `:ref="onMount ? (el: any) => onMount!(el) : undefined"` — an inline arrow reconstructed on every render, so Vue's setRef runs on every patch of the parent and `onDesktopLeftMount` is invoked on re-renders that have nothing to do with a pane change (App.vue re-renders on every colour tick through `cssColor`). The wrong-ref arm follows from PaneSlot's own documented one-rAF commit lag (PaneSlot.vue:65-73 and :95) read against a callback that samples `currentConfig.value.left` at call time (App.vue:324): the callback's notion of which pane it is holding comes from the NEW config while the instance handed to it can still be the OLD component. That is structurally sound but I did not capture the frame, so I mark it CONFIRMED-by-construction rather than measured, and I note it is moot under the cure — a `bindPane(slotName)` capture owned by usePaneRouter is a stable function identity that does not re-fire and cannot mis-attribute.

One sub-claim is false and I will not let it ride. Measured live on /#/ at 1440×900: h1 = 0, h2 = TEN, h3 = 11. The h2 elements are real and reachable — demo/scenes/about/AboutPane.vue:49 ('Detailed Guide') and five in demo/scenes/about/ColorNutritionLabel.vue (:18,:43,:71,:93,:149) — so 'no h2' is REFUTED. RESCOPED and FOLDED into D-4, with the false h2 clause struck from the record so no later close can cite it.

The edict violation is CONFIRMED: App.vue:164 is `import { ColorPicker } from "../picker"` — a value import — and its only use in the file is App.vue:223 `ref<InstanceType<typeof ColorPicker> | null>(null)`, a type position. Under `verbatimModuleSyntax: true` that emits a runtime import for something used only as a type, and `import type { ColorPicker }` would serve `InstanceType<typeof …>` identically. RESCOPED on consequence, because the challenger's stated harm does not exist: usePaneRouter.ts:21 imports ColorPicker as a genuine value and returns it from `componentFor` (:83), so the picker is in the eager graph regardless and the bundle delta of fixing App.vue:164 is zero. The row survives as a one-line hygiene correction the wave makes while it is already rewriting App.vue's import block, not as a bundle finding.

Confirmed, and the truth is worse than the accusation. App.vue:168-175 books a bundle-hygiene residual on the premise that 'the root `package.json` marks `./demo/**` side-effecting, so this eager-chunk barrel reach does NOT tree-shake the lazy sibling dialogs by static analysis'. I read the manifest: the root package.json declares `sideEffects: false` — nothing is marked side-effecting — and there is no demo/package.json to override it. The premise is simply false, so the residual it books is unfounded and the proposed reconciliation ('narrow the demo/** sideEffects glob') addresses a glob that does not exist. This is the same class as L-13: a structural rationale written in prose, never re-measured, and now load-bearing for a booked follow-up. The wave deletes the comment and the booking together rather than re-writing the comment, because a corrected comment is still an ungated claim.

The fact is CONFIRMED and I measured it in a virgin context with no storage: loading `http://localhost:9000/#/` settles at `http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(92%25+88.8+20+/+82.7%25)`, so every boot rewrites the address bar with a colour the user never picked. Mechanism: useColorUrl.ts:50-63's debounced `syncModelToUrl` calls `router.replace` on the first model tick, and the model is born from hydrate's default seed, so the default is immediately promoted into a shareable URL indistinguishable from a deliberate one. RESCOPED on the charge: I decline to book this against canon §6.2's frame-zero seed latch, because that entire `value-ground/3` contract is unimplemented — index.html declares no `data-ground-schema`, no `SeedToken`, no `--ground-seed` — so §6.2 is a program-level gap belonging to the ground wave, not an App.vue defect. What remains is the narrower and still true charge that the rewrite contradicts the 'born hydrated, ONE commit' law App.vue:225-230 asserts about itself.

CONFIRMED, and its second clause is the most useful sentence any challenger wrote about this component: the MT-F012 entry cure does NOT fix this. Creating main.ts moves the eight boot lines out of the HTML but leaves `<body class="relative" id="app" data-paper-field>` as both mount container and portal host, so the shell still cannot be instantiated anywhere else with its material intact and Vue still clears the body on mount. I acted on that clause: MT-W-APP-1's scope adds `<div id="app">` inside the existing body and re-points the mount, which is a three-line change that only makes sense while index.html is already open for the entry cure — exactly the coupling that justifies one wave rather than two. The row is the same defect as L-2 and D-9 seen from the boot side; all three carry as one, identifiers preserved.

CONFIRMED and materially stronger than accused. `grep -rln 'mount(' test/` returns ZERO files — no unit test in the repository mounts any component at all, let alone App.vue, so the vitest suite is structurally incapable of witnessing anything in this adjudication. The e2e half is exactly as charged: the two oracles that assert the overture DAG, e2e/smoke/oracles/o4-order-invariance.spec.ts (which reads `overture:b3` at :77 and `overture:b4` at :78) and e2e/smoke/oracles/o11-header-gates.spec.ts (:246), navigate only `page.goto("/")` — every `goto` in both files is `/` — which is the single route class where C-1 does not reproduce. The one oracle that could see the BLOCKER is pointed at the one route that hides it. This is L-12 in its purest form and it is why gate G3 is written per-route rather than per-app, and why the wave's ENV clause names what each environment is blind to.

result.dissent:
I dissent from CHALLENGE-D's gestalt, not from its evidence. D's framing is that every finding except D-5, D-6, D-9 and D-14 is a consequence of the dual-pane premise, "which is why the cure is a transposition". The measurements do not support that, and acting on it would produce the fourteenth arc wearing a wave's name. The two defects that actually break the product for a real user are NOT consequences of the two-pane premise: C-1 stalls the boot DAG on /#/gradient at any viewport, dual-pane or single, because the mount does not await router.isReady() — transposing to a single-scene shell would not touch it; and MT-F012 ships a blank production site because of eight inline lines of HTML that have nothing to do with panes at all. A transposition-first program would leave both live for however long eleven route compositions take, against a repository whose measured delivery rate is 38% and whose standing 193-wave formation sits at 2%.

I also dissent from CHALLENGE-D on evidentiary discipline in three specific places, and I record them because the same habit will recur. D-6 asserted nondeterminism from what was almost certainly a route-class confound; six trials refute it. D-15 correctly declared its own frame inadmissible and then asserted a "solid" source-side fact that the file contradicts in plain sight. D-4 bundled a canon-hard obligation (the H1, cited to §4.1 and §5.1) with an invented one (a skip link, which appears nowhere in the constitution and is not a conformance failure given nav+main), and a bundled accusation is one a close can discharge by fixing the easy half. CHALLENGE-C's C-4 did the same in reverse, asserting "no h2" against a page carrying ten. Each of these would have entered the registry as a finding had nobody re-derived it — which is precisely MT-F022's class, and the reason L-14 exists.

Where I dissent from CHALLENGE-L: it filed L-7 and L-14 under App.vue when neither is in App.vue, and L-9 as an edict violation when the edict says something else and the tree documents the choice. Subject discipline matters here more than usual, because a defect filed against the wrong component is a defect that the right component's wave will never see.

Finally, a dissent against my own convergence. My conclusions agree closely with the two juror seats already in area-core.json on C-1, D-1, D-2's citations and D-15. I read those seats only after completing my own derivation, and the agreement is on rows where the evidence is mechanical — a build hash, a mark list, a click that changes nothing — so I do not treat it as corroboration of anything except that mechanical facts are reproducible. The places where I differ from them are the places to examine: I refute D-6 outright (neither juror addresses it), I strike C-4's h2 clause and D-4's skip-link clause (neither juror separates them), and I decline to book C-7 against §6.2 because that entire contract is unimplemented. If worker-F converges with me on those four, the arbiter should ask whether we were genuinely independent before adopting either of us.

I set out to confirm this and the evidence inverted. The claim 'No rule applies a transform to .pane-shell' is false: PaneSlot's `<Transition>` applies its classes to the pane component's ROOT element, which for the picker IS `.pane-shell` (ColorPicker.vue:5), and both transition families set transform on it — `overture.css:65-67` `.overture-appear-from{transform:translateY(-12px) rotate(-0.6deg)}` and `animations.css:228-231` `.pane-wrapper--left > .vj-enter-enter-from{transform:translateX(-110%) rotate(-2deg)}`. Measured on a cold load, sampling `.pane-shell` every 40ms: classes `overture-appear-from+overture-appear-active` with a live `transform: matrix(0.999945, -0.0104718, …)` interpolating toward none, and — decisively — the interpolation CONTINUES after Vue removes both classes (`cls: ""` with matrix still settling), which can only be carried by the element's own declaration. Computed `transition-duration` on `.pane-shell` is 0.35s (`--spring-smooth-duration`) throughout, not `--overture-plate-land`: the scoped selector `.pane-shell[data-v-…]` (0,2,0) outspecifies `.overture-appear-active` (0,1,0), so ColorPicker.vue:399 is not dead residue — it is the governing clock of the plate arrival. There is a real finding buried here, but it is the opposite of the one accused: the picker's scoped rule silently overrides the overture's intended plate-land timing. Book that; delete nothing.

waveSpec.title: The readout stops writing — one writer, one formatter, one truth (delete the contenteditable headline path, its hex guard, and the multiplexed channel debounce)
waveSpec.scope: EXACT FILES, EXACT END STATE. (3) demo/color-session/useColorPipeline.ts — delete `updateColorComponentDebounced` (:209) and its export (:326); `updateColorComponent` (:190-207) stays and is the ONE channel writer. (4) demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/readoutReservation.ts — the shown-channel set becomes one source: the alpha entry at :96 either renders (alpha ≠ 1) or is deleted; headline cells ≡ rail cells (D-20). (5) NEW e2e/smoke/oracles/o28-readout-projection.spec.ts — the five gates below. waveSpec.structure: STRUCTURE, not gates, for three of the five rows (L-8). C-1/D-01: a Vue-controlled subtree cannot be made safely user-writable by any patch, so the writability is DELETED rather than validated — after this wave the readout has no `@input`, no emits and no editable descendants, and the defect class is unrepresentable in the component's surface. C-2: the multiplexed `debounce(updateColorComponent, 500)` is deleted, not keyed — with no debounced multi-argument writer in the pipeline there is no coalescing window in which one channel's intent can cancel another's; `debounce` in demo/shared/utils.ts keeps exactly one demo consumer (`parseAndSetColorDebounced`, single-argument, where coalescing IS the intent). C-10/C-12: both die as unreachable code with the handler that contained them. Only the projection-agreement property (G2) and the shown-channel parity (G5) need standing gates, because they are cross-file invariants no single type can carry today.

The assertion `innerHTML unchanged && hash unchanged` fails on both clauses.

gates.gate: G2 · PROJECTION AGREEMENT — after any independent write to the model, the readout text, the channel meters, `location.hash` and `document.title` all report the same channel values.
gates.command: npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o28-readout-projection.spec.ts --project=smoke -g "readout agrees with the model after an independent write"

NOTE this gate must contain an independent write; W48's existing 'agree in one settled routed frame' check is single-frame and would pass with C-1 fully present.

gates.gate: G3 · NO CHANNEL WRITE IS DISCARDED BY ANOTHER CHANNEL'S WRITE — two writes to different channels issued 120ms apart from the picker's channel editors both land in the model.
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: Navigate to `#/?space=lab&color=lab(80%25%2020%2030)`; write `30` to `l`, then 120ms later write `10` to `b`; wait 2000ms; read `location.hash`. The asserted property is driver-independent (it names the picker's channel editors by role, not by markup): after the cure the same test drives the two sliders, which call `updateColorComponent` directly and cannot coalesce.

gates.gate: G4 · THE READOUT IS A PROJECTION, NOT A HEADING OR A CONTROL — the readout element is not h1..h6, carries no `data-slot="card-title"`, and contains zero `[role="textbox"]` / `[contenteditable]` descendants; the route still has exactly one `<main>`.

Runs in both engines because I-20 forbids inferring webkit from chromium; the h1 clause is deliberately EXCLUDED (h1 = 0 on all 60 captures across all 15 routes — a shell-owned row, carried below, not this wave's to close).

TODAY (measured): rail ['92.0%','88.8','20.0','82.7%'] vs headline ['92.0%,','88.8,','20.0'] — the instrument is holding an 82.7%-alpha colour the headline does not describe, while readoutReservation.ts:96 budgets an `alpha` entry that `readoutLineCount`/`readoutFit` can never be called with.

Partial cure now: the shell half is unpinned; the composable's instantiation site is not.

waveSpec.title: Generate workbench — the save seam, the generation core's totality, and the vacuous oracle that certified them green
waveSpec.scope: Exact files, all verified to carry NO hash pin in CARRY-LEDGER §D: demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue (bind the second emit parameter; useTemplateRef; drop the redundant ?.() re-expose guards) · demo/color-session/generate-color.ts (exhaustive `never` arm in generateHues; total preset lookup with a named throw) · demo/styles/foundation.css (delete the two redundant `.generate-swatch` entries at :689 and :834) · demo/workbenches/generate/composables/useColorGeneration.ts (retire the dead @composables alias citation at :7) · demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts + demo/color-picker/App.vue (replace the six Ref<any>/ref<any> with a typed PaneActionSurface; delete the method-level ?. masks; delete the /generate dock action set that duplicates the plate verbs) · e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts (replace two vacuous assertions) · NEW test/generate-color.test.ts · NEW e2e/smoke/oracles/o21-generate-pin-residue.spec.ts. END STATE: the save seam persists the typed name; the generation core cannot silently return an empty palette; exactly one Regenerate seat exists in the DOM; the pane-action seam is typed so a renamed handler is a compile error; and every pin-locked defect is recorded EXECUTABLY rather than in prose. EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue, whose sha256 I re-verified this session as 4f95c57c7a6c46fa15a08b98b954a39529a12f71bda672423c7008c33ae324f6 — byte-identical to the CARRY-LEDGER §D glass BJ W4 receiver pin. Not one byte of it is touched, so the pin survives the wave intact.
waveSpec.structure: L-8 — four of the seven landing sites make a defect class unrepresentable rather than gating it. (1) generateHues gains a `default: { const _x: never = harmony; throw new Error(...) }` arm, so an unlisted harmony becomes a COMPILE error and can never again return a silent [] that save() would persist; the preset lookup gains a total form with a named throw. (2) PaneActionSurface replaces the three Ref<any> in usePaneRouter.ts:108-110 and the three ref<any> in App.vue:317-319, and the method-level ?. masks are deleted — after which renaming a handler is a type error rather than a silently dead dock button. I proved the witness can see this class: a scratch SFC compiled against tsconfig.demo.json returns TS2322 for `emphasis="not-a-real-emphasis"` (a KNOWN prop with a bad value) while accepting `variant="ghost"`, `tag="button"` and even `totally-made-up-prop` silently (UNKNOWN attributes) — so typing the seam is exactly what converts this defect class from invisible to checked. (3) Deleting the duplicate dock action set removes the second seat rather than asserting against it. (4) `.generate-swatch` is deleted from foundation.css because the producer's unconditional `.watercolor-swatch` class is already in both rule lists — one dead selector removed, no gate needed. GATES are used only where structure is unavailable: the save-name assertion (a runtime persistence property no type can express) and the pin-residue record (bytes this wave may not touch).

gates.gate: G1 — the saved palette carries the name the user typed
gates.command: npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts -g "the saved palette carries the typed name"
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY, measured live by me this session at 1440×900 with localStorage snapshot/restore: set input[aria-label="Palette name"] to ZZ-OPUS-ADJUDICATOR-NAME via the native HTMLInputElement value setter plus a bubbling `input` event, click button[aria-label="Save palette"], wait 900ms, read localStorage['color-palettes'] → palettes 1→2, the new entry's name is the literal "Generated Palette", storedContainsProbe:false, storedContainsHardcoded:true. Asserted product property: the persisted palette's `name` field equals the input's current value. It fails today because GeneratePane.vue:14 declares `function onSave(colors: string[])` — the second emit parameter is never bound — and :19 hardcodes pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", paletteColors).

gates.gate: G2 — the generation core is total over its declared domain
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY on two arms I reproduced on an esbuild bundle of demo/color-session/generate-color.ts under node: generatePalette(5, "bogus" as HarmonyName, …) returns an array of LENGTH 0 (generateHues :101-146 has a switch with no default) — a silent empty palette that save() would persist; and generatePalette(5, "nope" as PresetName, …) throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'l')` (GENERATION_PRESETS[preset] unguarded at :220, p.l[0] at :227) rather than a named error. The test asserts a named throw on both paths and length===count across all 10 presets × 6 harmonies × count 1..12. Additionally RED by absence: `grep -rln 'generate-color\|generatePalette' test/` returns EMPTY today — the module ships with zero unit coverage.

gates.gate: G3 — no per-component class duplicates a producer class in the global colour-fidelity lists
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: returns 2 (foundation.css:689 inside @media (forced-colors: active), :834 inside @media print). Expected 0. The deletion is provably behaviour-preserving, which is why this is a deletion and not a gate on the component: dist/watercolor-dot.js applies `watercolor-swatch` UNCONDITIONALLY (`class: l([c.value, "watercolor-swatch", e.animate && "watercolor-animated"])`), I measured the live className on the rendered swatch ending in `… focus-visible:outline-none watercolor-swatch`, and `.watercolor-swatch` is already present in BOTH lists. Paired DOM assertion in the same gate guards the premise. Note the corollary this kills: `[data-color-surface]` has ZERO producers repo-wide, so it is a dead selector and cannot be the migration target the challenger proposed.

gates.gate: G4 — no demo source cites a path alias that no longer exists
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: returns 1 — demo/workbenches/generate/composables/useColorGeneration.ts:7 cites `@composables/color/generate-color`, while the module's real import sits at :14 as `../../../color-session/generate-color`. The alias is provably dead: tsconfig.demo.json:32-34 records the W43/RF-15 kill in its own words, and no `@composables` mapping survives in any tsconfig or in vite.config.ts. Expected 0.

gates.gate: G5 — a renamed pane handler is a compile error, not a silently dead dock button
gates.command: grep -nE 'Ref<any>|ref<any>' demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts demo/color-picker/App.vue | wc -l  # expect 0; then rename regenerate→regen in GeneratePane.vue's defineExpose and run: npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit  # must exit NON-ZERO
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY on both halves. The grep returns 6: usePaneRouter.ts:108,109,110 (`generate|gradient|mix: Ref<any>` — and `grep -n any` on that file returns ONLY those three lines) and App.vue:317,318,319. And the rename typechecks GREEN today, because with the ref typed `any` the expression `paneRefs.generate.value?.regen?.()` is unconditionally legal TypeScript — I confirmed the baseline `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exits 0 on the current tree, and separately proved with a scratch SFC that this checker DOES report TS2322 on a typed member with a bad value, so the witness can see the cured state.

gates.gate: G6 — exactly one Regenerate seat exists in the DOM, counted outside the a11y tree
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY, and this gate exists because the CURRENT one is vacuous — the strongest L-2 finding in this corpus. My live count at 1440×900 over document.querySelectorAll('button') filtered by accessible label: TWO Regenerate seats — the plate's 144.8×40 visible pill, and a 32×32 dock action button whose computed visibility is `hidden`, nested in DIV.dock-face-content > DIV.dock-face > DIV.dock-crossfade — against a plate count of 1. The committed assertion at o20-generate-plate.spec.ts:38-40 compares page.getByRole('button',{name:'Regenerate'}).count() to the plate count; Playwright's getByRole excludes visibility:hidden elements, so it reads 1≡1 and certifies 'the orphan row is dead' while the duplicate sits one dock-face rotation away. The replacement counts DOM seats; it goes green when usePaneRouter.ts:191-201's /generate action set is deleted (unpinned).

gates.gate: G7 — the pin-locked residue is recorded executably, not banked in prose
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY by absence: the file does not exist, so the command exits non-zero with 'no tests found'. At close it holds one `test.fail()`-annotated assertion per pin-locked row, each with the RED input I measured this session: the swatch is a SPAN with pointerEvents:none and zero listeners (R1/R2); the three plate buttons all carry data-emphasis="secondary" plus a dead variant= attribute (R5/R9); the chrome row's child tops are 10 / 12.2 / 46.5 at 1440×900 (R12/R16/R30/R32); the rail paints stops at 0/25/50/75/100% while the thumb sits at 0.367 (R14); the count row's whole visible text is "5" (R17b/R33). A `test.fail()` test PASSES only while its defect persists and turns RED the instant the defect is cured — so this is the bank's re-trigger written as a command (L-4) and expressed as structure rather than prose (L-8). It cannot rot silently, and it forbids the string 'next tranche decides' from ever standing in for it.

GLASS-OWNED, relayed to the glass BH inbox as a fond, no local patch proposed: R29/R31 (thumb hit area) · R36/R38 (first-class gradient-track affordance). waveSpec.completableAlone: YES. The L-1 test — if this were the only wave that ever executed, would the tree be better and would the wave be closed? Every one of the seven gates goes green using only files I verified carry no hash pin, so the wave depends on no other wave, no producer release, and no owner ruling. The tree ends strictly better on facts that are independently checkable: a user's typed palette name is actually saved (a BLOCKER with a live user consequence, reproduced by me end to end); a shared colour module that had ZERO tests can no longer silently return an empty palette; the dock's silently-dead-button class becomes a compile error; a vacuous oracle that certified two BLOCKERs green is replaced by one that counts DOM seats; and two dead selectors plus one dead alias citation leave the tree. The pin-locked residue is not deferred — it is converted into executing tests that fail the moment they are fixed, which is the only bank shape L-4's own evidence shows surviving. Crucially the wave is also SAFE for the hold it inherits: GenerateControls.vue is not touched, so its sha256 still matches the CARRY-LEDGER §D receiver pin at close, and the glass BJ W4 v8 seam migration lands later against exactly the byte state it was promised.

result.dissent: Four places where I diverge from the challenger fleet, recorded for the arbiter to attack rather than adopt. (1) DISPOSITION INFLATION IS THE CORPUS'S MAIN DEFECT. Seventeen of the forty rows carry BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8, and I found the tag misapplied on at least six: the save seam (R3/R4/R6/R8) lands in GeneratePane.vue, the redundant class (R39) lands in foundation.css, the stale alias (R40) lands in useColorGeneration.ts, and the any-seam (R7/R22/R25) lands in App.vue and usePaneRouter.ts — none of which carries a hash pin. I re-read CARRY-LEDGER §D and it names exactly four receivers by sha256; only GenerateControls.vue among this component's files is among them. A hold on one file was read as a hold on a feature, which converted a one-line BLOCKER cure into a deferral. (2) CAUSATION ON THE SWATCH. R1/R2 book the inert dot as a glass debt. I disagree: glass 7 never declared a `tag` prop, and `inheritAttrs:false` on an aria-hidden decorative face is a defensible producer choice. The debt is entirely ours — a 6.x idiom left standing by the W44 adoption commit — and calling it a producer break routes the cure to a repo that owes us nothing. (3) WHICH REGENERATE DIES. R15 cites VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:194 ('Regenerate, Save/Publish and Copy live in ONE Dock control set') while the committed oracle o20 encodes the opposite T.W6 law ('the verb is plate chrome … the orphan toolbar row is DEAD'). That is a live canon conflict, not a defect, and I did not resolve it unilaterally. My wave deletes the DOCK set because that is the arm reachable outside the pin — but if the design synthesis rules for the dock, G6 stays valid and only its cure site moves. The arbiter should rule this explicitly rather than inherit my pin-driven choice. (4) THE FLEET GRADED ITS OWN WITNESS TOO KINDLY. No seat noticed that o20-generate-plate.spec.ts passes while two BLOCKERs ship underneath it — it reads the swatches only as paint (computed backgroundColor) and never as seats, asserts Save's VISIBILITY but never its EFFECT, and its orphan-count assertion is satisfied by a visibility:hidden dock button. A component with a committed oracle and 40 accusations against it should have had its oracle audited first; I would put that ahead of every remaining design row.
result.addendumClause: SCOPE AND HONESTY LEDGER. Corpus reconciliation: the brief said 37 accusations / 5 BLOCKER; I extracted 40 ledger blocks / 6 BLOCKER and cross-checked them against the raw returns — 39 records in registry/harvest/area-workbenches.json plus 1 in area-core.json, totalling 40, an exact match with no ledger row lacking a harvest ancestor and none dropped. The gap is duplicate rediscovery by seats blind to each other (the save seam appears 4×, the wrap 4×, the shim layer 3×, the perf claim 3×, the thumb 2×, the rail 2×), which under L-14 I treated as convergence evidence rather than noise; deduplicated, the corpus is 23 distinct claims. Tally: 26 CONFIRMED · 10 RESCOPED · 4 GLASS-OWNED · 0 wholly REFUTED. Zero rows were false end to end, but eight carried refuted sub-clauses which I enumerate so no close can cite them: the 16-ghost/15-outline breakdown (R5, actually 28 outline / 19 ghost / 2 primary-audacious / 1 destructive / 1 default, total 51 exact); '27 files use variant=' (R9, conflates legal Badge/Slider variant with illegal Button variant — 51 Button tags across 22 files); reka-ui reachability of an invalid preset (R11, no path exists); 'overflowing by exactly 3 px' (R12); 'four copies of the gradient computed' (R36/R38, two structural twins plus two one-liners); 'liveRegions: []' (R10/R27, one page-level role=alert exists); '[data-color-surface] already expresses the concept' (R39, zero producers repo-wide — a dead selector); and eight/nine /dom import sites (R28). Line citations drift by one at GenerateControls.vue:167/:177 and useColorGeneration.ts:7. ENVIRONMENT DISCLOSURE (L-12): the dev server at :9000 is UP and API-LESS — the only role=alert I found reads 'dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`', which is an environment fact and never counted as evidence; no data-backed surface (palette lists, admin panels) was judged. All live measurement is playwright-chromium, a SEPARATE cell from playwright-webkit and safari-app under I-20 — I inferred nothing across that line and marked R37's mobile-WebKit perf extrapolation UNVERIFIABLE-HERE for exactly that reason. Perf numbers are node/V8 against an esbuild bundle of the library core in isolation, which is the correct scope for auditing a comment that prices library generations, but is NOT a built-artifact measurement and no bundle or render claim rides on it. GLASS BOUNDARY HONOURED: four rows ruled GLASS-OWNED with no local patch proposed; I did not re-book any spectrum-seam visual row as a value.js defect, and I record that the prefix trap makes the Safari-capture evidence in R38 unable to separate engine interpolation from glass-owned blur — its source-level claim needs no screenshot and is what I confirmed. PIN INTEGRITY: I re-computed sha256(demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue) = 4f95c57c7a6c46fa15a08b98b954a39529a12f71bda672423c7008c33ae324f6, byte-identical to the CARRY-LEDGER §D receiver pin, and the wave is designed so it still matches at close. One structural risk I flag rather than bury: any future wave that DOES edit this file silently invalidates the glass BJ W4 receiver identity unless it re-pins the hash in the same commit — that is an unguarded bank-rot path in the hold itself, and it belongs in the next §D sweep. INSTRUMENTS: full source reads of GenerateControls.vue, GeneratePane.vue, useColorGeneration.ts, generate-color.ts, PaletteColorStrip.vue, usePaneRouter.ts, foundation.css rule blocks, o20-generate-plate.spec.ts, color-chips barrel and sample.ts, plus the glass-ui dist bytes for Button/Badge/Slider/WatercolorDot/useClipboard; one baseline `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` (exit 0); one purpose-built scratch-SFC typecheck experiment proving the checker sees bad values of KNOWN props (TS2322) but silently accepts UNKNOWN attributes including `variant`, `tag` and a nonsense prop — the mechanism claim of R5/R9/R1 turned from inherited assertion into measured fact; one esbuild bench-and-fuzz of the generation core; three live chromium probes at 1440×900 including a localStorage snapshot/restore reproduction that I restored cleanly. WRITES: none outside the scratchpad — no file under docs/tranches/V/megatranche/ was created by this seat, per the no-report-file instruction; this structured return is the deliverable.

THE COST-CLAIM CORRECTION IS BINDING ON THE CLOSE. No close of this wave may cite "two 32-sample ramp re-serialisations per drag frame" as a cured cost. Measured this seat, real WebKit drag, 8 pointermoves: movesReachingBarFromNonBarTarget=9, distinctRailRampWritesToDOM=8 — Vue's scheduler batches the two model writes per pointerevent into ONE flush, so serializer output reaching paint is 1x per move, not 2x. The double dispatch is real (onHandlePointerMove GradientStopEditor.vue:136-146 has no stopPropagation; onBarPointerMove :91-96 emits whenever draggingId is set; listeners at :206 and :266) and costs 2x emit + 2x eager stops.value.map() rebuild per event. Neither the challenger fleet nor this seat measured the serializer twice. A wave that claims a perf win it did not measure is MT-F012's class of vacuous close, and L-2 forbids it. SECOND CLAUSE: the wave may propose NO local glass-ui patch. WatercolorDot already ships as a published producer species at @mkbabb/glass-ui/watercolor-dot (verified in its exports; 19 demo files consume it), so D-6 is a CONSUME and BUILDS here; but L-13/D-14's cure — a variant="rail" or SliderThumb content slot on glass-ui's Slider — is a PRODUCER change, is GLASS-OWNED, and leaves this repository as a relay to the standing BH inbox fond plus the runnable bank in this spec. The masking-fallback ban applies: no local re-derivation of the producer's slider mechanics may be presented as the cure. THIRD CLAUSE: the coarse-cell evidence in G3a/G3b is playwright-webkit iPhone-14 ONLY. Per I-20 it transfers nothing to real Safari 26.4; a Safari claim needs safaridriver on :4599 as a separate evidence cell.
result.dissent:
1) ONE WAVE STRAINS L-1. I authored this as one wave because that was the brief, and the cures genuinely interlock (the leaf types module is what lets the ordering algebra be branded; the seat rail is what frees the meniscus for the add gesture and moves the remove verb off the drag axis; the single axis is prerequisite to both). But 22 confirmed rows across a 392-line component plus a 4-module model tree is large for the 38%-landing rate L-1 was written against. If the arbiter wants strict L-1 compliance the honest seam is TWO waves: (A) model + axis, gated by G2 (headless — no browser, no dev server) and G4 (static), carrying D-1 D-2 D-13 L-1 L-3 L-4 L-5 L-7 L-11 L-12 L-14; (B) the seat, gated by G1 and G3 (browser), carrying D-3 D-4 D-5 D-6 D-7 D-8 D-9 D-10 D-11 D-12 L-9 L-10. Both halves are individually completable and both are born RED today; (A) needs no browser at all, which is the stronger L-12 posture. I would ship the split.

2) I REFUTED PART OF D-11/L-9 AND NEITHER CHALLENGER NOTICED. See the addendum. Their own cited evidence (p3.mjs T9) counted handler invocations and never counted recomputes, then the row asserted recomputes. I measured it. This is the one place the challenger fleet asserted past its evidence.

3) I NARROWED D-5's AUTHORITY AND I THINK THE CHALLENGER PICKED THE WRONG CLAUSE. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1's "never color-only" clause is NOT violated — scale(1.25) is not a colour. The clause that IS violated, flatly, is the second sentence of the same bullet: "Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit." role null, aria-pressed and aria-selected both absent, and at exactly 2 stops the remove chip is suppressed (removable = stops.length > 2) so there is no third cue. A gate written against "colour-only" would have been unwinnable and wrong; G3c is written against the clause actually violated and is RED. Flagging because the same mis-citation may ride other components' D-rows.

4) I DECLINE TO CARRY L-2, L-6 AND L-8 INTO THIS WAVE AND I EXPECT DISAGREEMENT. All three are REAL and I re-derived all three to the byte. None is a GradientStopEditor defect: the component calls parseCssColor never, imports from demo/ui never, and resolves no value.js specifier at all. Booking repo-wide defects against a component wave is how a wave stops being individually completable — and how MT-F001 got attributed to a visual boundary instead of a parser one, which the challengers' own D-10 text names.

5) MY OWN PROBE FAILURES, RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. (a) My first gate-axis G1b arm read aria-label, which GradientStopEditor.vue:234 rounds to whole percent — it passed vacuously on a 0.2% error. I caught it, rewrote it to read style.left, and it went RED. A gate reading a rounded readout to assert sub-percent precision is L-2 vacuity in miniature. (b) My first figure-ground probe resolved oklch through getComputedStyle(.color) and produced garbage RGB triples (rgb(1,0,199)); I discarded its distances entirely and rest D-5 arm 1 on construction, not on that probe. (c) My first D-11 cost probe dispatched synthetic PointerEvents and got 0 rail writes — setPointerCapture rejects a synthetic pointerId — so I re-ran with real mouse events. None of the three broken outputs is cited anywhere in my verdicts.

verdicts.note: Re-derived live, WebKit 1440x900: bar x=224 w=462, border 1px each side. The ramp is a border-box layer (background-origin/clip border-box, size 100% 100%, GradientStopEditor.vue:317-326) so it paints 0% at x=224 and 100% at x=686. Handle centres ride calc(10px + (100% - 20px) * p/100) (:55-57) where the percentage resolves against the PADDING box (460px, origin 225): handle 0% measured cx=235, handle 100% cx=675 — 11px inboard at each end, 2.38% of the ramp span. My committed gate G1a prints the skew per handle: 0% -> ramp paints 2.381%; 100% -> 97.619%; interior stops -0.14% (45%), -1.15% (66%), -1.33% (86%); zero-crossing near 47%. G1c re-derives the user-visible consequence: a click at the pixel where the ramp paints 12% mints 10%, and 88% mints 90% — the challenger's p3 T6 numbers reproduce exactly. ATTEMPTED REFUTATION, PARTIALLY SUCCESSFUL AND RECORDED: the inset handle track is DELIBERATE and documented at :49-53 ('so the 0%/100% handles sit fully INSIDE the bar instead of hanging half off its rounded corners'), and the doc-comment the challenger calls a 'false claim' (:8-13, echoed at useGradientCSS.ts:258-262) is fairly read as asserting DIRECTION normalization — the rail always paints the 90deg projection at every type/direction — not endpoint alignment. That arm over-reads. The row survives entirely on its measured half: two coordinate systems for one domain quantity, neither derived from the other, diverging up to 2.38% of the instrument, with the add-ghost previewing a colour the ramp does not show at the pointer.

Re-derived live: from the default two stops, one bar click at 50% then a drag of the LEFTMOST handle to ~80% yields labels ['Gradient stop at 81%','Gradient stop at 50%','Gradient stop at 100%'] and CSS readout `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 81.2%, oklch(70% 0.165 205deg) 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)`. Computed --rail-ramp carries 37 sub-stops with 18 DESCENDING pairs, first14 = [81.2, 79.25, 77.30, 75.35, 73.40, 71.45, 69.5, 67.55, 65.6, 63.65, 61.7, 59.75, 57.8, 55.85]. Source: updateStop (useGradientModel.ts:127-131) applies no ordering policy; sampleCoalescedStops (useGradientCSS.ts:200) computes pos = s0.position + t*(s1.position - s0.position) over a negative range; GradientVisualizer.colorAtPosition:64-88 assumes sorted. SECOND ARM INDEPENDENTLY STRENGTHENED BY THIS SEAT, and it needs NO reorder at all: addStop (useGradientModel.ts:117-119) SORTS the stops array while the intervals array only grows at its TAIL via the length watch (:87-98). So inserting a stop in the middle silently re-pairs every downstream interval — an authored cubic-bezier on the pair a->c becomes the curve for a->b. My gate G2c asserts exactly this and is RED. The challenger framed it as index-keyed LABELS ('1 -> 2'); the real defect is that the authored EASING migrates, which is data loss, not a label bug. Re-derived on the COARSE cell (playwright-webkit, iPhone 14 descriptor; matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)') true, --touch-target 2.75rem, dpr 3, w 390) and it reproduces destructively. The remove control's painted box starts at offset 24, so offsets 14..22 are INVISIBLE and destructive'; and 'a tap 20px below the SELECTED handle's centre changed the stop count 3 -> 2'. A DIFFERENT arm from D-1 and it must not be folded in as a duplicate: D-1 is ramp-box vs handle-track; L-3 is border-box vs padding-box, with different magnitudes and different causes. Forward map (GradientStopEditor.vue:75-81): origin = rect.left = 224 (BORDER box, getBoundingClientRect), span = rect.width - 20 = 442. Inverse map (:55-57): `calc(10px + (100% - 20px) * p/100)` where, for an absolutely-positioned child, 100% resolves against the PADDING box = 460 with origin 225. They are not inverse. LIVE PROOF, my committed gate G1b, RED today: I clicked the bar at x=235 — the exact pixel at which the 0% handle is painted, at clientY = railTop+4 so the bar owns the gesture — and it minted a stop whose inline style is `left: calc(0.2% + 9.96px)` and whose measured centre is cx=235.88, 0.88px to the RIGHT of the pointer that created it. Forward-map arithmetic: (235-224-10)/442*100 = 0.226% -> quantised 0.2%. The error is antisymmetric, 0 at 50%, +/-0.23% at the ends. Note for the gate author: the aria-label rounds to whole percent so this arm is INVISIBLE to any assertion that reads the label — my first draft of G1b passed vacuously for exactly that reason and I rewrote it to read style.left.

waveSpec.title: The gradient rail becomes one axis, one ordered model, one seat species
waveSpec.scope: EXACT FILES. Re-authored: demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientStopEditor.vue (392 lines today). New leaf modules: demo/workbenches/gradient/model/types.ts, model/stops.ts, model/sample.ts, model/literal.ts, and demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useRailGeometry.ts. Edited: composables/useGradientModel.ts (types move out; the re-export block at :20-29 is deleted; addStop/updateStop/removeStop delegate to the stops algebra; setStopsFromColors validates), composables/useGradientCSS.ts (imports types from the leaf; emits the interpolation-space clause; sampling delegates to model/sample.ts), composables/gradientParse.ts (imports types from the leaf; consumes clamp from @mkbabb/value.js/math; its non-decreasing reject branch becomes unreachable-by-construction), composables/useGradientInterpolation.ts (the second re-export shim at :13-17 is deleted), GradientVisualizer/GradientVisualizer.vue (colorAtPosition:64-88 deleted; the :color-at prop and the @select handler deleted; INTERPOLATION_SPACES/HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS imported one-hop from color-session/color-space-meta exactly as MixConfigBar.vue:18 does; the selected-stop inspector lands here), GradientPane.vue (the dead cssColorOpaque injection at :8 is either wired to the inspector or deleted). EXACT END STATE. (1) ONE position axis: the ramp and the handle track are the same coordinate system, expressed once, in pixels, built on clamp+scale from @mkbabb/value.js/math, with the handle half-width read from the rendered box rather than re-declared as a JS literal. (2) ONE ordered model: a branded readonly OrderedStops producible only by model/stops.ts (insertStop / moveStop, which re-sorts stably / removeStop); serializeGradient, sampleCoalescedStops and parseGradientCSS all take OrderedStops; intervals are keyed by the stop PAIR, not by array index. (3) ONE seat species: each stop is a named geometric button seat carrying a WatercolorDot face (consumed from @mkbabb/glass-ui/watercolor-dot, already used in 19 demo files), sitting on a quiet rail BENEATH the meniscus, carrying role/aria-valuenow/min/max/valuetext-with-ordinal and an explicit selected state; the remove verb leaves the rail for the selected-stop inspector, which also lands colour and numeric-position entry. (4) ONE sampling law with an exported home, emitting linear-gradient(<dir> in <space>, ...). (5) ONE gesture owner: the drag lives entirely on the captured handle; the bar's pointermove serves hover only. EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE with reasons in the verdicts: L-2 (parser band), L-6 (demo-wide import surface), L-8 (build/toolchain), L-13 and D-14 (glass-ui producer change — relay and bank only). NO file under src/, api/, test/ or e2e/ is edited except e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts, whose cross-drag blindness is named in CARRIES.
waveSpec.structure: L-8 STRUCTURE OVER GATES, STATED PER DEFECT CLASS. Made UNREPRESENTABLE by structure (no gate can decay because the wrong state cannot be written): (a) non-monotonic stops — a branded readonly OrderedStops with a single producer module means updateStop cannot express an unsorted list, and the parser's reject branch becomes unreachable rather than a runtime tripwire aimed at the app itself (D-2, L-1); (b) two coordinate systems — one useRailGeometry(el, halfPx) exposing toPosition(clientX) and toOffsetPx(position) over ONE box, with the handle positioned in px, makes the two directions provably inverse and leaves no second axis to declare (D-1, L-3, D-13); (c) two sampling implementations — model/sample.ts exporting sampleAt(model, p) and sampleRamp(model) leaves no concept for a component prop to carry, which simultaneously deletes the optional-collaborator masking fallback (L-4, L-11); (d) two selection channels — deleting the select emit leaves one wire (D-12, L-10); (e) the type cycles and the dead barrel — a leaf model/types.ts with zero intra-tree imports inverts the dependency and lets the barrel be deleted, which is why it lands FIRST (L-7, L-5); (f) the untrusted literal sharing a shorthand with its own fallback ground — separating the checker into its own layer means an invalid value cannot clobber the fallback (D-10); (g) hand-rolled range arithmetic — importing clamp and scale from the published subpath leaves nothing to re-derive (L-12); (h) two literal grammars — a single formatColorLiteral used by the mint, the parse fallback and the readout (L-14). GATES ARE UNAVOIDABLE, and are therefore written, only for: the a11y/keyboard contract (G3c, G3d — no type asserts that Home moves a handle), the coarse hit-region disjointness (G3a, G3b — a geometric fact about rendered boxes), the block-axis reservation (G3e), the add-affordance budget (G3f), and the axis agreement itself (G1 — the ramp is painted by CSS, which no TypeScript type reaches).

gates.gate: G1 — the rail has ONE position axis (D-1, L-3; D-13 rides here)
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY, exit 1, output pasted verbatim from this seat's run: 'G1a Gradient stop at 0%: model 0% but the ramp under its centre paints 2.381% (skew +2.381%, tolerance +/-0.25%)' / 'G1a Gradient stop at 100%: model 100% but the ramp under its centre paints 97.619% (skew -2.381%)' / 'G1b clicked the exact pixel at which the 0% handle paints; the forward map minted 0.2% (expected 0% +/- 0.15%) — the forward and inverse maps are not inverse (border box vs padding box)' / 'G1c click at rail fraction 12% (the pixel where the ramp paints 12%) minted a stop at 10%' / 'G1c click at rail fraction 88% ... minted a stop at 90%'. THE INPUT THAT MAKES IT RED: the DEFAULT two-stop gradient at 1440x900 — no interaction is needed for G1a. The ramp is a border-box layer spanning the full 462px box (GradientStopEditor.vue:317-326) while handle centres ride calc(10px + (100% - 20px) * p/100) over the 460px PADDING box (:55-57), and the forward map takes its origin from getBoundingClientRect().left = 224 with span rect.width - 20 = 442 (:75-81). IT WOULD GO RED AGAIN IF: the handle box is resized without updating HANDLE_HALF (D-13's latent arm — this is the gate that catches it), a border or padding is added to .gradient-rail, or the ramp is re-inset without re-insetting the click map. GATE-VACUITY NOTE, recorded because it nearly shipped: G1b's first draft read aria-label, which GradientStopEditor.vue:234 rounds to whole percent, and therefore PASSED on a 0.2% error. verdicts.id: D-1 (BLOCKER · focus indicator is the user's raw alpha-bearing colour)
verdicts.note: Re-derived on all four legs and I could not break any of them. SOURCE: ColorInput.vue:16 carries `focus-visible:outline-none` verbatim; :162-166 `inputStyle` returns `{borderColor: 'var(--destructive)'}` when `parseError` is true and `{borderColor: cssColor.value}` when focused — the error branch returns FIRST, so error+focus erases the focus indicator entirely, exactly as accused. LIVE (my own chromium 1440x900 probe against dev :9000, arm `focused`): after a real `el.focus()` the field reports `activeIsInput: true`, `outline: "rgb(0, 95, 204) none 1px"` (outline-style NONE — the UA ring is suppressed) and `inlineStyle: "border-color: lab(92 88.8 20 / 0.827);"` — the indicator IS the user's colour including its alpha. The contrast arithmetic needs no probe: a border painted in the same colour family as the field's own measured background rgb(251,250,248) reaches 1.00:1 at `#fbfaf8` and vanishes outright at alpha 0 (`oklch(0.7 0.1 200 / 0)`), against the WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 floor of 3:1 — and alpha 0 is reachable by dragging the app's own alpha slider. FORCED-COLORS: I read foundation.css:702-720 directly — the `:where(...)` restoration roster is `a[href], button, [role="button"], [role="combobox"], [role="tab"], [role="slider"], [role="menuitem"], [role="option"], input, select, summary, .rail-handle, .rail-remove-chip, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`. Neither `[role="textbox"]` nor `[contenteditable]` is a member, and my live attribute enumeration of the element returns exactly `[data-v-55dadc03, contenteditable, role, aria-label, class]` — no tabindex. `el.matches(roster)` measured **false** for the field and **true** for the send button. The bitter half is also true: `SAFE_ACCENT_KEY` is injected at :157 and spent on the arrow glyph's stroke at :74 and :81 while the raw alpha-bearing `cssColor` takes the focus boundary. Nothing here is glass-owned — every line is value.js's.

verdicts.id: D-2 (MAJOR · `.btn-interactive` resolves to no CSS rule)
verdicts.note: I attacked this from four directions and it survived all four. (1) `grep -ro 'btn-interactive' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/ | wc -l` → **0**, with the installed version confirmed `7.0.0` by reading the package.json. (2) I widened the search past `dist/` to the WHOLE package — `grep -rl 'btn-interactive' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/` → **no files at all**, so it is not hiding in a preset, plugin or source tree. (3) It is not defined demo-side either: the only 8 non-markdown hits in `demo/` are 5 template class strings (ColorInput.vue:69, :78; CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:75, :78, :100) and 3 comment lines asserting the contract. (4) LIVE, my probe on the rendered button: `transitionProperty: "all"`, `transitionDuration: "0s"`, `scale: "none"` — no hover leg, no press leg, no focus register, no disabled opacity. The entire disabled treatment is ColorInput.vue:344-346 `cursor: not-allowed`. The false-record half is confirmed too: demo/DESIGN.md:247 records the row as `landed` and ColorInput.vue:61-66/:327-334 spend ~15 lines asserting a contract that is measurably not in effect. Refutation attempt that FAILED for me: I checked whether the atom might be a producer rename — glass 7.0.0 DOES ship `tap-squish` (12 hits) and `focus-ring` (87 hits), so the substitute exists and the cure is a local consumption change, not a producer ask. No masking fallback is proposed and no glass patch is needed; a BH relay is optional courtesy, not a dependency.

verdicts.id: D-3 (MAJOR · the one nameless button on the route, 24x24, type=submit)
verdicts.note: Independently re-measured, and it reproduces to the character. My own live enumeration of `/#/` at 1440x900 returns `buttonsTotal: 26` with exactly ONE button having no aria-label, no text and no title: `{cls: "send-btn btn-interactive", type: "submit", w: 24, h: 24}` — the accused element, at the accused size, with the accused default type. Source confirms both branches: ColorInput.vue:67-75 and :76-82 are `<button class="send-btn btn-interactive">` whose only child is an SVG, and the Loader2/ArrowRight swap at :73-74 means the in-flight state is equally nameless with no `aria-busy`. The independent cross-check holds: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md §namelessButtons records `safari-desktop-light /#/: 1` and `safari-desktop-dark /#/: 1`, and §smallTapTargets records `safari-desktop-light /#/: 8` — I read both rows myself. ONE SUB-CLAIM RESCOPED WITHOUT CHANGING THE VERDICT: I grepped for a `<form>` ancestor across ColorInput.vue, ActionBarLayer.vue and Dock.vue and found none, so `type="submit"` is inert in practice — it is a latent hazard (any future form wrapper turns every click into a page-level submit) rather than a live failure. The accessible-name defect is the substance and it is unqualified: 24x24 is also below the 44px target floor that PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-12 prescribes an invisible seat for.

verdicts.id: D-4 (MAJOR · error badge occludes the send button and carries zero semantics)
verdicts.note: Re-measured end-to-end by my own probe after driving `lab(#)` into the live field, and the load-bearing number is exact. Badge rect [676.375, 777.344] width 100.97; send rect [757.344, 781.344] width 24.0; computed **overlap 20.0px = 83.3% of the button** — the accused figure to the decimal. The mechanism is source-certain: ColorInput.vue:337 `.send-btn { right: 0.25rem }` vs :350 `.error-badge { right: 0.5rem }`, both `position: absolute` against the same physical edge, and I measured `z-index: auto` on BOTH, with the badge later in DOM order (template :86-90 follows the buttons at :67-82) — so the badge wins the paint every time, by construction, not by chance. Semantics measured live while the error was displayed: `aria-invalid` null, `aria-describedby` null, `aria-errormessage` null, `aria-multiline` null on the field; `role` null and `aria-live` null on the badge; `pointer-events: none`. A screen-reader user is told nothing. ONE FIGURE CORRECTED, AGAINST THE ACCUSER'S FAVOUR: the accusation says the badge covers 66% of a 153px field; at my viewport the field measured 118.7px and the badge 101.0px, i.e. **85%** — the occlusion is viewport-dependent and was UNDERSTATED, not overstated. The button-overlap ratio is the stable, geometry-fixed number and it is 83%.

verdicts.id: D-5 (MAJOR · ~2.04s trailing debounce, no live preview, silent on retry)
verdicts.note: All three legs are source-decisive and I re-derived each rather than trusting the timing trace. (1) `useColorParsing.ts:92` is literally `const parseAndSetColorDebounced = debounce(parseAndSetColor, 2000);` and ColorInput.vue:199 is the ONLY `@input` handler — there is no second, faster preview path, so a trailing 2000ms timer is the entire feedback budget and every keystroke resets it. Human typing at ~1 char/s therefore yields ZERO preview for the whole entry, exactly as accused; the ~2.04s trace is just the timer plus a frame. (2) `useColorParsing.ts:62` is `if (!input || input === previousInvalid) return;` — a dedup cache guarding a PURE function, and I proved its consequence mechanically rather than by eye: the committed harness's fifth test (`npx vitest run --config docs/.../probe.vitest.config.ts`, re-run by me → **5/5 green, 10ms**) drives the real composable and shows the second identical invalid string early-returns with `parseError === false` and `console.warn` never called. The natural human retry loop — type it again — is a total no-op. (3) `useColorParsing.ts:54-58` clears `parseError` on a 2000ms `setTimeout`, so error truth lives on a timer rather than being derived from the current value; the badge vanishes while the field is still invalid. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-08 rules this family ADD-AFFORDANCE.

verdicts.id: D-6 (MAJOR · MT-F001/MT-F024 laundered into user-blaming copy, invisible to telemetry)
verdicts.note: This is the design-axis face of the same disease as L-1; I confirm it on its own evidence and record the merge rather than double-counting it into the wave. Re-derived against the CURRENT `dist/subpaths/css.js` — which was REBUILT TODAY (Jul 27 11:52, newer than the challenger's Jul 24 14:04 artifact), so this is a genuinely fresh measurement, not an inherited one: `oklch()`, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `lab()`, `lch()`, `color()`, `oklab()`, `hsl(  )` all THROW `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`, while `oklch(` → `{ok:false, diagnostics:[{code:'css_syntax', start:0, end:6, expected:['color'], actual:'oklch('}]}` and `notacolor` → ok:false. The crash is NARROWER than the clean failure path and therefore invisible beside it. Throw site re-located by grep: `src/css/grammar.ts:181 const components = splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g, " "), "space");` — the `!` is false because `splitTopLevel("", "/")` returns `[]`. Swallow site: `useColorParsing.ts:84` is a BARE `catch {` with no binding, and it renders the constant literal at ColorInput.vue:88. LIVE in the running app, my own probe: typing `oklch()` yields `{text: "oklch()", badge: "not a valid color", errClass: true}` with **pageErrors: []** — the only console error on the page is the dev-config CORS warning, which is an ENVIRONMENT fact and not this defect. The audit's own `pageErrors: 0` is manufactured, exactly as accused. The `initialParse` gate at :50/:86 is real but the harness's own comment honestly notes it is burned during boot by ColorPicker.vue's inputColor watcher — I adopt that correction: `previousInvalid`, not `initialParse`, is the silencer that bites a real user.

verdicts.id: D-7 (MAJOR · contenteditable <span> where glass-ui `Input` is already re-exported)
verdicts.note:
Every consequence the accusation names, I reproduced myself. The primitive genuinely exists and is genuinely already in this tree: `demo/ui/input/index.ts` is the single line `export { Input } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/forms";`, `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/input/` ships `Input.vue.d.ts`/`types.d.ts`, and I read `InputProps` verbatim — it offers autocomplete, class, defaultValue, disabled, enterkeyhint, form, inputmode, invalid, maxlength, minlength, modelValue, name, pattern, placeholder, readonly, required, size, type. The accused prop list is accurate. Measured consequences from my live probe: (a) PLACEHOLDER — `el.innerHTML='
'` → `el.matches(':empty')` **false**; `el.innerHTML=''` → **true**. Browsers leave a `

(b) MARKUP — `el.innerHTML='rebeccapurple!'` survives verbatim, `querySelectorAll('*').length === 2`: the value channel accepts arbitrary markup. (c) `aria-multiline` measured null on a `role="textbox"`. (d) No inputmode/enterkeyhint/maxlength/pattern anywhere on the element (attribute census: data-v, contenteditable, role, aria-label, class). verdicts.id: D-8 (MAJOR · element-level mask-image used as a text fade)
verdicts.note: Source and computed style agree exactly, and the mechanism argument is correct rather than merely stylistic. ColorInput.vue:299-301 sets `--input-action-width: 2.5rem` and `mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, black calc(100% - var(--input-action-width)), transparent 100%)` on `.color-input` itself; :303-306 sets `mask-image: none` on `:focus`. My live measurement: `maskImage: "linear-gradient(to right, rgb(0, 0, 0) calc(100% - 40px), rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) 100%)"`, `paddingRight: "36px"`, `textAlign: "center"`. A mask applies to the ELEMENT, not to its text — so the field's own `border-color: var(--input)` (:295) and its `bg-background` are faded to transparent over the right 40px along with the ink, which is why the right border and corners pop back into existence in one frame when focus removes the mask. The two gutter numbers are genuinely unrelated: 40px of mask against 36px of padding (`pr-9`) against a 24px button (measured). And the fade is physical-right under `text-align: center`, so the value is centred while only one end is faded. The redundancy leg is also true: :16 carries `text-ellipsis whitespace-nowrap`, so two truncation idioms are stacked on the same box. Nothing here is glass-owned.

verdicts.id: D-9 (MAJOR · dead prop, dead defineExpose, dead injections, a third Copy path)
verdicts.note: I re-ran every grep myself rather than trusting the transcript, and every one returned what was claimed. `grep -n "editTarget" demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue` → **only :139**, the prop declaration; the parent supplies it at ActionBarLayer.vue:118 (`:edit-target="editTarget"`), so a value is threaded in and never read. `grep -rn "copyAndSetInputColor|onSubmitColor|submitProposedName" demo/` excluding the file itself → **zero matches**, so three of the five `defineExpose` members at :282-288 have no reader anywhere in the demo. `grep -n "colorInputRef" demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue` → **only :28 (declared) and :116 (bound)** — the ref is created and attached and never dereferenced, so `focus` and `inputIsFocused` are unreachable too: the entire exposed surface is dead. `cssColorOpaque` (:146) and `canProposeName` (:150) are destructured from the injected model and never appear again in the file. `copyAndSetInputColor` (:219-223) pulls glass-ui's `writeClipboard` in to implement a third Copy path while my own live 26-button enumeration shows `aria-label="Copy color"` already owned by ActionToolbar — PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-13 rules Copy `total 2→1` and this is an uncounted third. The god-module observation is measured, not rhetorical: the file is **377 lines** and `proposeMode` forks :196-201, :203-211 and :252-267 — two value types, two submit semantics, two error vocabularies in one component.

verdicts.id: D-10 (MAJOR · crown hover magnification never animates; hover-only; tooltip on a non-focusable <svg>)
verdicts.note: The load-bearing leg is decisive from the SERVED stylesheet, which is stronger than the computed-style trace the accusation leaned on. I pulled the compiled utility out of the live document myself: `.hover\:scale-110 { &:hover { @media (hover: hover) { --tw-scale-x: 110%; --tw-scale-y: 110%; --tw-scale-z: 110%; scale: var(--tw-scale-x) var(--tw-scale-y); } } }` — Tailwind v4 writes the **`scale` longhand**, which is not `transform`. ColorInput.vue:35 declares `transition-[opacity,transform]`, so the transitioned property set and the animated property set do not intersect: opacity fades over 200ms while the magnification snaps in one frame. This is the identical F3 'spatial-on-bezier stray' that this file's own comment at :327-334 claims was retired from `.send-btn`, surviving two elements away. `@media (hover: hover)` removes the affordance entirely on coarse pointers. The tooltip leg is source-certain: `TooltipTrigger as-child` at :32 forwards to `<Crown>`, a lucide `<svg>` with no tabindex — not focusable — while TooltipContent :42-57 carries the colour's approved NAME, CONTRIBUTOR and CSS, i.e. real meaning, not decoration. ENV LIMIT DISCLOSED (L-12): dev :9000 is API-LESS, so `currentColorMeta` never populates and my probe measured `crownPresent: false` — I could not take the live `getComputedStyle(<crown>).transitionProperty` reading. I did not need it: the class string and the compiled utility settle the mechanism without a rendered crown. The crown's live arm is UNVERIFIABLE-HERE and must ride a seeded fixture or the API-up stack; the verdict does not depend on it.

verdicts.id: D-13 (MAJOR · absent from the DOM at mobile, two-step disclosure on desktop)
verdicts.note: I tried hardest to refute this one, because 'absent at rest' is the classic lazy-mount false positive — and I failed to refute it. My first probe reproduced the accusation (`.color-input` present at 1440x900, **null** at 390x844). So I wrote a second, adversarial probe that DRIVES the disclosure at mobile with `isMobile: true, hasTouch: true`: rest → `.color-input` absent; click `[aria-label="Toggle action bar"]` → still absent, and the full button census after the click contains no `Open color input` control at all (Save edit, Cancel edit, Switch to slug, Generate new slug, Cancel, Select view, Toggle action bar, Picker, About, Menu, Login, @mbabb, Select color space, l/a/b/alpha channels); a further attempt at the input step → still absent. There is no gesture I found at 390x844 that produces the product's only free-text CSS-colour entry. The desktop half is equally confirmed and worse than stated: my ancestor walk at rest shows `.color-input` itself at `visibility: hidden`, its wrapper hidden, the `.dock-layer-grid` **inert**, and `.dock-face` **inert + aria-hidden="true"** — so at rest the control is hidden AND removed from the accessibility tree behind two disclosures. Corroboration from the audit's own record, which I read directly: REPORT.md §namelessButtons has `safari-desktop-{light,dark} /#/: 1` and NO `/#/` row for either mobile matrix, and that single nameless button is this component's send button — a second, independent proof of the mobile absence. SUBJECT NOTE: the defect is real but its cure lives in the dock composition (Dock.vue / ActionBarLayer.vue), not in ColorInput.vue, so it FOLDS to MT-DOCK-LAYERS-1 with its id preserved and its own born-RED gate — not a deferral.

verdicts.id: D-11 (MINOR · type roles outside the constitution's closed matrix at two sites)
verdicts.note: The subject survives; one supporting leg is an artifact and I correct it rather than inherit it. My own in-page role probes: `.color-input` = **Fira Code 18.608px / 27.912px**; `text-mono-small` (the constitution's value/code role) = Fira Code 16.4/22.96; `text-small` (control/label) = Plus Jakarta Sans 16.4/22.96; `.error-badge` @apply text-xs (ColorInput.vue:353) = Plus Jakarta Sans 12/16. I read VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:78 directly and it does declare the matrix 'closed across all eighteen compositions' with only P019's Picker pair exempt, mapping values/code/provenance to `text-mono-small` or `mono-caption` + Fira Code. So `.color-input` — which carries the `fira-code` FAMILY class and no SIZE role class at all, landing on the inherited 18.608px root size — belongs to no matrix row, and `text-xs` appears nowhere in the matrix. CORRECTION, made against the accuser: the accusation cites `mono-caption` as a Plus-Jakarta-18.608px matrix row. My probe returns exactly that, but the reason is that a bare `mono-caption` class does NOT resolve in the demo (glass-ui's registration emits `.75rem` + uppercase + tracking, and my probe span showed neither) — the measurement is the inherited default, not a role. That leg should be dropped from the record; it does not carry the finding. The finding stands on `.color-input` ≠ text-mono-small and `.error-badge` = text-xs ∉ matrix. Consequence worth keeping: the 27.912px line-height is what drives the field's measured 45.91px height and therefore the whole dock band.

verdicts.id: D-12 (MINOR · propose-name success and failure both invisible)
verdicts.note: Source-decisive and re-read line by line. ColorInput.vue:242-244 is exactly `} catch (e: any) { console.warn("[ColorInput] Failed to propose name:", e?.message); }` — a durable, user-initiated, network-backed operation whose only failure record is the console, which no user has open. The success path at :237-241 clears `proposedName` and repaints `innerText` from `formattedCurrentColor` with no confirmation of any kind — the user cannot distinguish 'your name was submitted' from 'the field reset itself'. The only operation state is `proposing` (:227), and it has no visual treatment at all because `.btn-interactive` resolves to nothing (D-2, independently confirmed) — so even the in-flight state is invisible apart from the Loader2 glyph swap, which itself has no accessible name (D-3). The `catch (e: any)` in a `strict: true` codebase is a real, separate hygiene defect: `unknown` is the correct binding and `e?.message` needs a narrowing. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 ('persistent operation state stays with the entity/workspace') and PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-08 (ADD-AFFORDANCE) both rule this family. UNVERIFIABLE-HERE caveat recorded but not verdict-changing: dev :9000 is API-LESS, so I could not drive a real `proposeColorName` round-trip; the defect is entirely legible from the two code paths and needs no round-trip to establish.

verdicts.id: D-14 (MINOR · physical offsets throughout; no LTR isolation on a technical value)
verdicts.rescopedTo: CONFIRMED as a source-verified physical-geometry + missing-isolation inventory (the accusation's own directly-verified half). The RTL visual-reordering consequence is UNVERIFIABLE-HERE and is recorded as a stated hypothesis, not a finding — no RTL locale is reachable in-app today.
verdicts.note: The accuser was already honest here — its reproduction field literally reads 'NONE — hypothesis for the visual reordering' — and my job is to hold the rescope rather than let the hypothesis ride the confirmed inventory into the wave as though it were measured. CONFIRMED HALF, all re-read by me at HEAD: `pr-9` (:18), `right-2` (:35), `.send-btn { right: 0.25rem }` (:337), `.error-badge { right: 0.5rem }` (:350), `mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, …)` (:300) — five physical-axis offsets, zero logical properties; and my live attribute census returns exactly `[data-v-55dadc03, contenteditable, role, aria-label, class]` — no `dir`, and my computed read returns `direction: "ltr"`, `unicodeBidi: "normal"`, i.e. no `unicode-bidi: isolate` on an element whose entire value vocabulary is technical LTR (`#rrggbb`, `oklch(… / …)`, slugs). Combined with the measured `textAlign: center` this is, as accused, the worst of both: a technical LTR string centred in a container whose direction the document may flip. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1 is quoted accurately (chrome/nav/layout follow logical direction; CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance render in LTR-isolated spans). UNCONFIRMED HALF: that a value beginning with `#` or `/` visibly reorders while the model keeps the original bytes. That is a correct reading of the bidi algorithm but it is a prediction, and the environment cannot witness it. Both halves enter the wave — the inventory as a BUILD with a mechanical gate, the reordering as a bank whose re-trigger is 'the first RTL locale arm'.

verdicts.id: D-15 (MINOR · Parse-Lab AST + gamut verdict gated behind a 300ms hover-only popover)
verdicts.note: Source-certain, and I checked the one thing that could have refuted it. ColorInput.vue:3-8 is `<Popover trigger="hover" :close-delay="0" :open-delay="300">` with the whole field as its `PopoverTrigger` (:9), and the content at :94-110 is NOT decoration — it is the serialized current colour plus `<ParseEchoReadout />`, which I opened and read: it injects `astEcho` and `gamutVerdict` from `COLOR_MODEL_KEY` and renders the space, the per-channel AST parts and the sRGB gamut verdict. That is instrument data, and PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 6 ('subtraction precedes explanation') plus PR-14 rule the species. THE REFUTATION I ATTEMPTED: perhaps glass's Popover opens on focus in hover mode, giving keyboard users a path. It does not — I read `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/popover/Popover.vue.d.ts` and `PopoverTriggerMode = Extract<Trigger, "click" | "hover">`: there is no focus mode in the producer's type at all, and the docstring calls hover a 'fine-pointer hover preview'. So there is no keyboard path and no touch path, by the producer's own contract. GLASS BOUNDARY HELD: the defect is value.js's COMPOSITION choice (putting instrument data behind a pointer-only disclosure whose trigger is the text field the user must approach to click), not a glass deficiency — `trigger="click"` exists and a persistent readout region exists in the Picker. No producer ask, no local patch to glass, no masking fallback.

verdicts.id: L-12 (MAJOR · seat L-b · `crown-appear` is dead by construction)
verdicts.note: This is the cleanest kill in the corpus and I confirmed it with two independent instruments, both mine. (1) I curled the compiled scoped stylesheet the dev server actually serves — `http://localhost:9000/@fs/…/ColorInput.vue?vue&type=style&index=0&scoped=55dadc03&lang.css` — and read the emitted CSS: it contains `@keyframes crown-appear-55dadc03 { … }`, hash-suffixed by Vue's SFC compiler, and for contrast it contains the correctly-rewritten class-driven sibling `.color-input-mode-flash[data-v-55dadc03] { animation: input-mode-flash-55dadc03 … }`. Vue rewrites `animation` declarations INSIDE the style block; it does not touch template `style` attributes. (2) I took a live keyframe census of every CSSKeyframesRule in every reachable stylesheet on the running page: **54 names**, containing `crown-appear-55dadc03` and NOT containing `crown-appear`. The inline reference at ColorInput.vue:38 (`animation: crown-appear var(--duration-panel) var(--ease-decelerate) forwards;`) therefore resolves to nothing, on every device, in every browser, and always has. No global fallback exists: `grep -rn "crown-appear" demo/` returns exactly three hits — :38, :369, and demo/DESIGN.md:213 (prose) — and `grep -n crown demo/styles/animations.css` returns nothing. The pairing is unsatisfiable by construction: a scoped `@keyframes` is consumable only from a class rule in the same block; an inline `style` attribute is consumable only against a GLOBAL keyframe. This also correctly refutes the prior pass's own negative proof ('the animation law is honoured') — the seat caught its predecessor, which is exactly the behaviour L-14 exists to produce. Violates owner edict 6 (an animation deleted by construction rather than by decision) and edict 5 (per-instance inline override where a root class belongs).

verdicts.id: L-13 (INFO · zero negative-space coverage for the degenerate functional body)
verdicts.note: Re-derived exactly. `grep -rn 'oklch()\|"lab()"\|rgb()\|hsl()' test/` returns **nothing** — the input class that crashes the published parser has no assertion anywhere in the suite. Only six test files mention `parseCssColor` at all, and I enumerated them myself: test/v4-c1.test.ts, test/v4-css-public.test.ts, test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts, test/ink.test.ts, test/preview-chips.test.ts, test/view-accents.test.ts. The contract this leaves unguarded is real and public: `src/css/types.ts` declares `ParseResult<T> = {ok:true,…} | {ok:false, diagnostics:[ParseIssue,…]}` and package.json:4 says 'failure-explicit' — I read both. So a throw could be (and was) introduced and shipped invisibly on a failure-explicit public surface. verdicts.id: L-16 (MINOR · seat L-c · the Parse-Lab echo echoes the committed model, not the parse)
verdicts.note: Source-decisive on both sides of the wire, and I read both files. `useColorParsing.ts:94-96`: `const astEcho = computed(() => { const color = model.value.color; const parts = PICKER_CHANNELS[color.space].map(…) })` — there is no reference to the source string, to a parse result, or to any diagnostic anywhere in the computed; it is a formatter over the LAST COMMITTED model. `ParseEchoReadout.vue` (which I opened) injects `astEcho` and `gamutVerdict` from `COLOR_MODEL_KEY` and renders the space plus per-channel parts plus the sRGB verdict, under a comment at ColorInput.vue:107-109 that calls it 'the Parse-Lab echo (AST + gamut verdict)'. The defensive-catch census is real: I counted `grep -rn "} catch {" demo/ | wc -l` → **47** repo-wide, with the twelve cited sites around picker-color calls verified. THE REFUTATION ATTEMPT, which is the actual work here: I wrote a probe under the committed harness and ran `serializePickerColor` over nine degenerate but CONSTRUCTIBLE colours — hsv(0,0,0), hsv with a 'none' hue, kelvin at both domain ends (1000 and 40000), ictcp(0,0,0), jzazbz(0,0,0), rgb('none','none','none'), oklch with alpha 'none', rgb with alpha 'none'. **All nine serialized successfully** (e.g. `oklch(0% 0 none)`, `rgb(none none none)`, `oklch(65.925…% 0.230… 35.205…deg)`).
