waveSpec.structure: STRUCTURE, not gates, on five of the six defect families (L-8). (1) The Result stops being transposed: `parsePickerColor` returns `ParseResult<CssColor>` and the discriminant survives to the render. `catch {}` cannot swallow what is never thrown — the bare-catch class becomes unrepresentable on this path rather than lint-forbidden, and the 'user typo vs library crash' confusion is killed by the type, not by a rule. (2) The primitive swap makes six defects unrepresentable at once: glass-ui `Input` owns its own focus register (so D-1's `focus-visible:outline-none` + user-colour border has nowhere to live), is a real `<input>` (so it is a member of foundation.css:702-720's forced-colors roster by element name — no roster edit, no local override), carries its own role tokens (D-11), scrolls its own overflow (so D-8's element-level mask deletes rather than being tuned), refuses markup and honours `:empty`-free placeholder semantics natively (D-7 a/b/c/d), and preserves native undo/redo because nothing writes `innerText` imperatively any more (D-7 e). (3) The component split makes the god-module smell unrepresentable: two value types, two submit semantics and two error vocabularies stop sharing a `proposeMode` boolean, and every dead exposed member (D-9) has no home to survive in. (4) `previousInvalid` is DELETED, not tuned — it is a cache guarding a pure function, and deleting it removes the class of 'the second identical attempt is a total no-op' rather than shortening it. (5) The keyframe law is made structural by a mechanical gate over the whole demo, not by fixing one line: if the reference is inline, the keyframe must be global; if the keyframe is scoped, the reference must be a class in the same block; no third combination is legal — and G4 enforces it repo-wide so this cannot recur in the next component. WHERE A GATE IS UNAVOIDABLE AND WHY: the accessible-name / hit-target / ARIA-wiring properties (G2, G3) cannot be made unrepresentable in Vue templates — nothing in the type system forbids an unnamed button — so they take runtime gates. The 44px seat and the 0px error/action overlap are geometry, which only a rendered page can assert. INTERIM CATCH, declared as a debt with a runnable exit: because π owns grammar.ts:181, `parsePickerColor` must, for now, wrap the library call in ONE named catch that reports the fault and returns a distinct `internal_fault` discriminant. That is not a bare swallow — it reports, it discriminates, and it is deleted the moment B2's re-trigger fires.

WHY IT IS A WAVE AND NOT AN ARC: the nineteen BUILD rows are not nineteen changes. Thirteen of them fall out of ONE substitution (contenteditable span + hand-rolled button → glass-ui `Input` + a named action + an in-flow message node), and the remaining six fall out of ONE boundary change (`parsePickerColor` returns its Result). result.dissent: DISSENT AND UNRESOLVED TENSION, preserved rather than ruled away. (a) SEVERITY OF D-1 (BLOCKER). I confirm the finding without reservation but I contest its rank relative to L-1. D-1 is a WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 conformance failure with a reachable worst case (alpha 0 → the indicator is literally invisible) and no forced-colors fallback — genuinely serious. But it degrades an affordance; L-1 delivers a library CRASH to the user as copy blaming their own typing while telling the product's telemetry nothing, and it does so on the one surface where a human types CSS into a CSS library's own demo. If only one can be first, L-1 is first. I record this as ranking dissent, not as a downgrade: both are BLOCKER-weight and both BUILD in this wave. (b) WHETHER MT-COLORINPUT-1 IS ONE WAVE OR TWO. I argued myself into one wave on the coupling (D-4's cure cannot be written without L-1's cure, because you cannot render `diagnostics[0].expected` through a bare catch that destroyed it), and I stand by that. But I want the disagreement on the record: a reasonable arbiter could split it into MT-COLORINPUT-1 (the field substitution, 13 rows) and MT-COLORINPUT-2 (the parse boundary, 6 rows), accept a temporary generic error string in the first, and get two smaller certainly-completable waves instead of one probably-completable one. Given that the measured landing rate across 22 tranches is 38%, that argument deserves an answer rather than a dismissal. My answer is the coupling; I do not claim it is the only defensible one. (c) THE INTERIM CATCH IS A DEBT I AM UNCOMFORTABLE WITH. Because grammar.ts:181 belongs to π, this wave's `parsePickerColor` must wrap the library call in one named, reporting catch that returns an `internal_fault` discriminant. That is defensible — it reports, it discriminates, it never blames the user — but it is still a catch on a path whose whole point is that catches were the disease. It exists only because of a cross-band ownership boundary, and B2's re-trigger (`node --input-type=module -e \"import('./dist/subpaths/css.js').then(m=>{try{m.parseCssColor('oklch()');process.exit(1)}catch{process.exit(0)}})\"` flipping from exit 0 to exit 1) is the command that must delete it. If that bank is never swept, this wave will have replaced a bare swallow with a polite one, and the polite one will outlive its reason. (d) L-17'S BEHAVIOURAL ARM MAY YET BE TRUE. I refuted it as unsubstantiated after nine constructible degenerate colours all serialized cleanly, and I stand by refusing to let an unreproduced double-append enter the wave as measured fact. But absence of a constructible throw across nine hand-picked candidates is not proof that none exists — a fuzz over the AnyColor space could find one, and if it does, the row's severity rises from latent hazard to live data corruption. I did not run that fuzz; I am recording that I did not, rather than implying the space is closed. (e) D-13's OWNERSHIP, softly contested. I fold it to MT-DOCK-LAYERS-1 because the cure lives in Dock.vue/ActionBarLayer.vue, not in ColorInput.vue. But a reader could fairly say the defect IS ColorInput's — a control that does not exist on mobile is a fact about the control — and that folding it out of this component's only wave risks it never being decided. The gate I wrote for the fold is my hedge against that; if MT-DOCK-LAYERS-1 does not carry it verbatim, this row should come back here.

Residual disagreements, preserved for the arbiter: (i) severity ordering — I would rank the D-5+L-1 previousInvalid compound (the retry total-no-op) as the worst LIVED harm, above D-1's contrast failure, because it hits every user of the feature within seconds while D-1 requires specific colours or assistive contexts; D-1's BLOCKER class nonetheless stands on accessibility law and I do not move it; (ii) the fleet's '3 BLOCKER' headline double-counts one identity (both L-axis passes filed the same defect) — the true count is 2 blocker identities; (iii) D-6's proposed seat-level cure ('report the internal fault distinctly') and L-1's proposed cure (no try anywhere — let the TypeError become a page error) are in direct tension for the interim period before the parser band lands; my wave rules for the typed-and-loud seam over the uncaught crash (a shipping demo must not white-screen on 'oklch()' while the root fix awaits another wave's landing), and I flag this as a genuine judgment call the arbiter may overturn; (iv) UNVERIFIABLE-HERE was needed nowhere: every data-independent claim was decidable from source/dist/toolchain, and the one API-dependent arm (propose success) is explicitly scoped to a mocked assertion in the wave rather than left unadjudicated.
